title: Sugargoo Spreadsheet: Check Live Listings Before Ordering
dek: Verify the seller, product ID, exact variant, price and photo source before ordering from a Sugargoo spreadsheet. Keep a dated record for warehouse QC.
label: Spreadsheet field guide

sections.heading: Start with a live listing, not a confident label
body: A Sugargoo spreadsheet helps you discover products and compare possible purchases. It does not establish that stock is current, a seller will send the pictured version, or a product will fit. Treat a row as a research lead. The useful question is not whether a list calls an item trusted, but whether you can trace the current listing, exact option and evidence behind that claim.

This independent catalogue links to product routes outside the site. A destination may itself be another directory rather than the original seller. Follow the route until you can identify the marketplace and seller. Keep the original row for comparison. If a button now opens a different product, a similar photograph is not enough to assume that the listing still represents the same item.

sections.heading: Record identity before price
body: Create a short record containing the marketplace, seller name or identifier, product ID, complete URL and date checked. Titles are weak identifiers because sellers can edit them and different shops can reuse the same photograph. A product ID is more useful, but only together with its marketplace and seller context. Keep these fields separate so a changed title does not silently become a new purchase.

Check the source page independently from the agent import screen. One can work while the other fails. A login screen, unavailable preview or import error does not by itself prove that a product is sold out. Note the precise failed step and follow the [link troubleshooting guide](/articles/sugargoo-spreadsheet-links-not-working) before replacing the address. Never replace an uncertain route with an unverified lookalike.

sections.heading: Match the exact variant and available stock
body: A listing can contain several models, colours and sizes under one address. The spreadsheet thumbnail may show only one of them, while the displayed starting price belongs to another. Select the intended option and compare its thumbnail, seller wording, size system, model code and price. If the agent imports incomplete options, resolve the missing information before payment instead of assuming a default will be correct.

Stock belongs to a particular option at a particular moment. A visible product page does not establish availability of your size. Save the selected option and any seller restriction with the order notes. If manual ordering is supported for that listing, provide an unambiguous description and reference image, and check the current acceptance and return conditions. Manual entry cannot make an unsupported product eligible.

sections.heading: Use reference prices to shortlist, then check the total
body: Compare seller prices in CNY where possible. The dollar figures on this site use a fixed illustrative conversion of ¥6.72 per US$1; they are not a live exchange-rate feed or a checkout promise. The payment conversion, domestic delivery, service fees and optional work can change the amount you pay. International shipping is a later cost and should have its own budget.

Write down the amount for the exact option, quantity and domestic freight shown before confirming the order. A low headline price may describe the cheapest accessory rather than the pictured product. If a figure changes between the directory and checkout, investigate the difference. Keep the original reference and the confirmed amount separately so future readers do not mistake an old estimate for a current quote.

sections.heading: Label the source of every photo
body: Seller photos describe an offer; warehouse photos record an item that arrived for an order. A community image may show somebody else’s purchase, a different option or an earlier batch. These are different kinds of evidence. Label each image with its source and date where known. Do not describe a catalogue photograph as QC simply because it looks detailed or appears beside a product link.

An external QC example can help you decide which questions to ask, but it cannot verify your future item. If the original order context, variant or date is missing, say that the match is unconfirmed. The [QC photo guide](/articles/how-to-read-sugargoo-qc-photos) explains how to compare your own received item against the order record without turning photographs into an authenticity or durability guarantee.

sections.heading: Choose size using measurements with matching definitions
body: A familiar size letter or number is only a starting point. Read whether the chart describes body measurements, garment measurements, foot length or another dimension. Compare like with like, using a comfortable item you already own where appropriate. Record the unit, measuring position and seller’s stated tolerance. A measurement without its method can create more confidence than the evidence supports.

For footwear, do not interchange foot length, insole length and outsole length. For a hoodie, distinguish a flat chest width from a full circumference and check body length as well. Use the [shoe measurement guide](/articles/sugargoo-shoe-size-guide-measurements) or [hoodie sizing guide](/articles/sugargoo-hoodie-sizing-measurements) to prepare a specific request. A warehouse ruler photo can inform the decision, but it cannot guarantee comfort or how fabric behaves after wear.

sections.heading: Plan the warehouse check before arrival
body: Identify the uncertainty that could change your purchase decision: the selected label, a critical dimension, accessory count, visible seam or a specific colour detail. Standard photo coverage and optional services can change, so check the options offered for your current order. Ask for an observable fact, not a broad instruction to judge whether the product is good. One precise question is easier to answer.

When photos arrive, start with product identity and quantity, then inspect overall condition and finally the important detail or measurement. Keep a dated note of what is confirmed and what remains unresolved. Request additional evidence while the applicable seller return or exchange process is still available. Warehouse storage time is a separate clock and should not be treated as an extension of the seller’s return window.

sections.heading: Check parcel implications before building a large basket
body: An item can be inexpensive to buy and expensive to send. Packaging, weight, dimensions, fragile parts and product attributes affect the available routes. Before adding several similar items, check whether the exact destination and goods are accepted. Batteries, liquids and other attributes may need special handling; use the current route information rather than a general promise from a spreadsheet.

The [shipping page](/shipping) illustrates actual and volumetric weight. Its result is a planning comparison, not a live freight quote. Compare packed dimensions and the rules of the actual service before paying. For a US destination, the [USA quote comparison guide](/articles/sugargoo-shipping-to-usa-quote-comparison) explains how to hold destination, contents and package assumptions constant so a cheaper-looking quote does not hide a different service or excluded charge.

sections.heading: Keep a field-level verification record
body: A useful row can distinguish “source page opens”, “variant checked”, “price checked” and “own-order QC received”. These events do not happen together. Record the date beside each field instead of applying one broad verified badge to the entire product. If a source is unavailable, mark that field unconfirmed and keep the last known value as history rather than presenting it as current.

When a seller changes an option or a link is replaced, preserve the previous identity and explain the change. This allows somebody reviewing warehouse photos later to understand what was actually ordered. Store account numbers, addresses and private payment details outside any public spreadsheet. Share only the evidence needed for the product comparison, with personal order information removed from public screenshots.

sections.heading: Finish with a decision you can explain
body: Before payment, confirm the current seller route, exact variant, total at the purchase stage, evidence source, planned QC request and plausible shipping route. If one important fact is unresolved, write it down and decide whether to wait, ask a precise question or choose another item. The purpose of a checklist is to expose the missing decision, not to make every row look complete.

After arrival, compare the received item with that saved record before approving international shipment. Keep the source, selected option, photos, measurements and decision together. This process cannot remove seller, carrier or fit risk, but it makes changes visible and gives support a clear explanation if something differs. A smaller shortlist with traceable evidence is more useful than a large collection of unexplained links.

title: Sugargoo QC Photos: Match the Listing Before Shipping
dek: Match warehouse photos to your seller listing and ordered variant, request useful measurements, and document unresolved differences before international shipment.
label: QC inspection handbook

sections.heading: Know what a QC photograph can establish
body: Sugargoo QC photos can show the visible condition of an item received for an order. They may reveal a wrong colour, missing accessory, damaged panel or size-label mismatch before international shipping. They cannot by themselves establish authenticity, fabric composition, internal construction, long-term durability or comfort. Begin with the question the photograph can actually answer rather than treating a clear image as a general quality certificate.

Check the photo coverage and optional services shown for your current order. An older guide or another buyer’s screenshot may describe different angles or conditions. This guide provides an inspection method, not a promise about the number of photos or services included. Your goal is enough relevant evidence to decide whether the received item matches what you ordered, while the applicable after-sales process is still available.

sections.heading: Connect the image to the live listing and saved order
body: First confirm the order reference, marketplace, seller, product ID and selected variant. Match the size, colour, model and quantity before examining small construction details. A technically good photograph of another order cannot verify your purchase. Keep a source listing screenshot from the time of payment because the seller may later alter the available options, images, description or price without preserving your original view.

Open the live listing to check its current identity, then compare it with the saved order record. If it has changed, describe the difference rather than silently using the new page as your purchase reference. The [spreadsheet guide](/articles/sugargoo-spreadsheet-guide-2026) explains which fields to keep. When the link itself fails, use the [link troubleshooting steps](/articles/sugargoo-spreadsheet-links-not-working) and retain the original product ID instead of substituting an unrelated page.

sections.heading: Separate seller, community and own-order photos
body: A seller image supports a claim about an advertised product. A community QC image may help identify a question, but it might concern another size, seller, date or batch. Your own warehouse image is evidence about the item attached to your order. Label these categories clearly in a comparison folder. Do not describe someone else’s photo as evidence that your future purchase will arrive in the same condition.

For an external example, record the original source, known variant and date, and say when any of these are unknown. Avoid collecting cropped images that lose their context. A matching background or similar packaging is not a reliable identity check. If sharing your own record publicly, remove names, addresses, account identifiers and other private details while retaining the product information needed to understand the comparison.

sections.heading: Inspect overall shape and condition first
body: Use front, back and side views to check the largest features: silhouette, panel alignment, paired items, quantity, stains, holes, crushed areas and missing components. For shoes, compare left and right together; for clothing, compare sleeves, shoulder lines and pockets; for bags, inspect handles and the overall structure. Identity and a major defect matter more than a tiny cosmetic detail in an otherwise attractive photograph.

Camera position can make one side appear larger or hide a surface. Look for the same concern in more than one angle. If the apparent problem could be perspective, ask for a centred photograph on a flat surface. Keep the original image as well as any marked copy so support can see both the location of the concern and the full item it belongs to.

sections.heading: Treat colour and close-up detail cautiously
body: Lighting, white balance, reflections and your display can change perceived colour. Compare several angles and the selected colour label before deciding that a shade is wrong. If tone is crucial, ask whether a neutral-light photograph with a simple white or grey reference is available. Such a photo improves comparison but still does not turn a screen into a calibrated colour measurement.

Inspect stressed seams, zipper ends, sole edges, straps, graphics and hardware. Distinguish a loose thread from an open seam, or a reflection from a scratch. Request a closer, square view when detail is blurred. Enlarging or sharpening a tiny crop cannot recover information that was never captured. Labels and markings can help identify the order, but their appearance alone does not establish authenticity.

sections.heading: Ask for measurements with visible endpoints
body: A useful measurement request names the item, dimension, unit and measuring method. Ask for both the starting point and endpoint of the ruler to be visible, with the product positioned appropriately and without deliberate stretching. Compare the result with the seller’s chart using the same definition and any stated tolerance. A number without context is less useful than a clear photograph showing how it was obtained.

For footwear, keep foot, insole and outsole measurements separate; see the [shoe size guide](/articles/sugargoo-shoe-size-guide-measurements). For clothing, distinguish flat width from circumference and use the [hoodie measurement guide](/articles/sugargoo-hoodie-sizing-measurements) to compare chest, length, shoulder and sleeve. Compare against an item you own where appropriate. Measurements reduce uncertainty, but materials, shape and construction still affect fit.

sections.heading: Write one actionable extra-photo request
body: Instead of “please check quality”, state an observable task: photograph the left pocket seam straight on; show both size labels together; or measure a removable insole from heel to longest toe. Identify the order and exact area, attach an annotated reference if the interface allows it, and explain which uncertainty the requested view should resolve. Check availability and any fee before ordering optional work.

Avoid combining several ambiguous requests into a vague message. If the returned image does not show the necessary endpoint or angle, explain that missing element rather than restarting the discussion with a general complaint. Keep the request and response together. This record helps distinguish a measurement you actually received from an assumption made while interpreting an overview photograph.

sections.heading: Decide while the relevant return process is available
body: Review QC promptly. Warehouse storage duration and seller return eligibility are different conditions, and a long storage allowance does not preserve every return option. Check the current order status, seller terms and support instructions for your item. If there is a material mismatch, describe it early using the saved listing, ordered variant and warehouse evidence. Do not wait until parcel preparation to identify an already visible problem.

Separate a wrong order, a material defect and an acceptable cosmetic variation. Your preferred remedy may be an additional check, exchange or return, but availability and costs need confirmation for that order. Record what was requested, who needs to act and any deadline given. Keep seller return charges, service charges and possible refunds distinct rather than assuming every payment will automatically be reversed.

sections.heading: Keep a comparison record with unresolved fields
body: Use a compact record with the order reference, source product ID, selected variant, photo date, observable finding and next action. For example, “size label matches; length still unmeasured” is more precise than “QC passed”. Record a result only when the image supports it. A missing view should remain unknown; it should not become a positive check merely because no defect is visible from another angle.

For electronics, photographs may show the model, plug or accessory count but cannot establish battery capacity, electrical safety or long-term function. Ask whether an appropriate supported test exists if that question matters, and understand its limits. Keep such functional uncertainty separate from visible condition and from shipping eligibility. A product that looks correct may still have attributes that restrict the available international routes.

sections.heading: Approve the parcel as a separate decision
body: After the item is acceptable, review packaging, protection, packed dimensions, destination and the current route conditions. Removing a shoe box may change parcel size but also changes protection and what you receive. Decide deliberately and record the instruction. The [shipping guide](/shipping) explains weight planning, while the [USA quote comparison](/articles/sugargoo-shipping-to-usa-quote-comparison) helps compare equivalent assumptions when that is your destination.

Save the original warehouse photos, listing, selected variant, measurements and final instructions before shipment. Name the record by order and date so a later delivery issue can be compared with the pre-shipment condition. QC review cannot eliminate every product or transport risk. Its practical value is a documented decision: what matched, what remained uncertain, what action was taken and why you chose to proceed.
